title: Null result: attn-only-2l does not perform induction on repeated random tokens
label: null result: behaviour absent, no mechanism
behavior: Claimed: when shown a sequence of random tokens that then repeats, the 2-layer attention-only model predicts the next token of the repeat correctly (dataset task 'induction').
summary: The claimed behaviour does not exist in this model (local-full, full precision). On 320 induction prompts across two seeds the model got 0 correct. The mean log-probability of the correct token is -11.13, slightly below what a uniform guess over the 48,262-token vocabulary would give (-10.78). Showing the model the first copy of the sequence gives no measurable benefit over replacing it with unrelated tokens: the clean-minus-corrupt gap was +0.19 nats on seed 0 (n=64) and -0.02 nats on seed 1 (n=256). The investigation stopped after the baseline step because there is no behaviour to explain; no circuit is claimed and no verification was run.

claims.text: The model does not predict the next token of the repeat: top-1 accuracy is 0/64 (seed 0) and 0/256 (seed 1) on local-full at full precision.
The correct token gets a mean log-probability of -11.13 on both seeds, slightly below the uniform level of ln(48262) = -10.78, so the model has no preference for the correct token.
The first copy of the sequence does not help: clean-minus-corrupt log-probability is +0.19 nats on seed 0 and -0.02 nats on seed 1; the small seed-0 gap did not replicate.

limitations: Only the supplied 'induction' dataset format was tested (BOS + 12 random tokens + the first 11 repeated, 24 positions). Other sequence lengths or natural-text repetition were not tested.
No internal experiments (attribution, patching, attention patterns) were run, by design: with a clean-vs-corrupt difference of about zero they would only characterise noise.
The seed-0 pre-registered prediction (accuracy >= 0.5, taking the task statement at face value) was refuted; this is the central finding, not a miss to explain away.
Why the model fails (for example whether its weights are untrained) was not measured and is not claimed here.
open_questions: Is this checkpoint untrained or the wrong file? A weights_svd of W_E / W_U or a baseline on ordinary text would tell.
Does a different checkpoint of the same architecture do the task? If so, rerun this investigation against it.
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null result: behaviour absent, no mechanism

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model performs induction as described: on repeated random-token sequences it predicts the next token of the repeat correctly on most prompts.

prediction.statement: Top-1 accuracy on the clean (repeated) prompts is at least 50%; chance is 1/48262.
